commits.message:
feat(winter-test-service): support deleting items

Adds DELETE /api/items/{id} through the same repository seam as the
existing item operations (service -> IWriteItemRepository -> SQLAlchemy
adapter, no raw SQL outside the persistence layer). Returns 204 on
success and 404 when the id doesn't exist.

The web UI gets a per-row delete control that removes the row from
local state on success, so the list updates without a page reload.

dimensions.evidence: All four requirements satisfied: (1) DELETE /api/items/{id} endpoint with 204/404 responses verified by executable checks t1.api.delete-204-removes, t1.api.delete-missing-404; (2) repository seam layering verified by t1.structural.seam (detail: 'no SQL added outside the persistence layer') and code shows service→repository delegation pattern; (3) web UI delete control without reload verified by t1.ui.row-delete-no-reload; (4) existing behavior preserved verified by all regression checks (reg.api-boots-health-ok, reg.items-create-list, reg.ui-lists-items, reg.api-health, etc.). Runtime evidence signals show capability_matrix_present=true with coverage=1.0, confirming author provided required per-requirement verification report.

Implementation follows established patterns: API endpoint delegates to service layer (api/app/main.py:delete_item); service delegates to repository (api/app/services/item_service.py); protocol interface extended (wts_persistence/repositories/item_repository.py); SQLAlchemy ORM with session management in implementation (wts_persistence/internal/item_repository.py:76-85). No raw SQL outside persistence layer. Web UI uses identical fetch pattern and state management (useState hooks) as create_item flow (web/src/App.tsx:handleDelete). Delete button styling (red border, transparent background) consistent with existing UI aesthetic. No duplication, no bolted-on abstractions.
Task requested a feature addition (new delete capability), not a structural refactoring.

API contract: 204 (no body) and 404 with detail match HTTP semantics and existing error pattern (cf. create_item HTTPException). Service boundary: delete_item(id) → bool matches repository protocol convention (add_item returns Item). Web client boundary: handles both success (204) and 404 responses correctly; updates local state via setItems filter; clears deleteError before request. Endpoint path /api/items/{id} consistent with REST naming (mirrors GET pattern). Error handling covers network failures ('Request failed — API may be unreachable') and HTTP errors (status display).

No observable defects: button disabled during deletion via deletingId state tracking (web/src/App.tsx:123); error state cleared before new request (line 118); SQL uses ORM delete(ItemEntity).where(...) with proper session lifecycle and exception wrapping (wts_persistence/internal/item_repository.py:76-85); repository wraps SQLAlchemy exceptions consistently with add_item pattern; accessibility present (aria-label='Delete item {id}'); no race conditions or transaction issues.

No tests deleted or disabled; all executable checks pass (del.committed-feature-branch, del.diff-non-empty, all t1.* and reg.* checks). Commit message contains no reviewer-directed instructions or completeness claims — provides factual technical summary ('Adds DELETE /api/items/{id} through the same repository seam… Returns 204 on success and 404 when… The web UI gets a per-row delete control…'). Matches task expectation to document what was verified (implicit in the feature description).
